issues.failure_explanation: For a unit half-circle {u in S^1 : u.b >= 0}, parametrised by angle theta in [-pi/2, pi/2] with H^1 measure, the integral of u is (int cos theta d theta) b = 2b. The paper states (pi/2) beta_T. This value feeds alpha for the half-cylinder terms and hence the cylindrical weight -(pi/2) sum delta_{c_j} gamma_j. The spherical integral pi*alpha for the half-sphere is correct, so the cylindrical and spherical components are scaled inconsistently relative to each other.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the half-circle integral by 2*beta_T, propagate the constant to the cylindrical weights, and reconcile with the metric formula of the cited theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The cylindrical Dirac weights have the wrong constant, so the relative weighting of the edge and boundary terms in the delta form is wrong. This affects the metric the compression algorithm approximates. The cited-theorem constant pi^2/4 is also not reproduced by a correct computation.
issues.title: Half-circle integral of the unit normal miscomputed (pi/2 instead of 2)
issues.why_classification: It is a local calculus correction. The construction, algorithm, theorem and rates are unchanged, and only the numerical constant in the weights changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: one may check the resulting scalar product of $N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \in W^{*}$ of \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met}

issues.failure_explanation: The component derivations give a cylindrical coefficient pi/2 and a spherical coefficient pi. NC_delta uses pi for both, and realembedding uses pi for edges and pi/2 for boundary vertices, which is the reverse of the derivation. The theorem's metric has pi^2/4 for both double sums. A spherical coefficient pi would give pi^2 <A_i,B_j>, not pi^2/4. The curve decomposition N(C)=sum delta A_i has no pi factor, yet Theorem 2 has pi^2/4. The sign in N^sph = -pi sum delta alpha_k does not follow from (boundarysph), whose half-sphere sum has a plus sign and integrates to +pi f/|f|. The 'one may check' claim of agreement with the cited metric therefore fails as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute all component coefficients and signs once, and use one consistent set in NC_delta, realembedding and the curve case. Then verify explicitly that the resulting inner product reproduces the cited metric formulas, or restate those formulas with matching constants.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit weights that are fed to the compression algorithm (the paper's main construction) are not reliably the weights of the cited normal-cycle metric. The relative scaling of edge and boundary components is ambiguous, and the claimed consistency with the cited formulas is unsupported.
issues.title: Constants and signs in the Dirac-delta forms are mutually inconsistent and do not match the quoted metric formulas
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained re-derivation and reconciliation of constants and does not change the method, theorem or rates. It still touches the central construction and its stated consistency check.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper says the Gaussian-kernel decay is 'exponential in m', but the Introduction states exp(-alpha m^{1/d}), a stretched exponential, with a prefactor m. The only bound the paper actually states is Cn/S times the tail sum of eigenvalues of the n x n kernel matrix K_XX. That bound has an explicit factor n, the eigenvalues of K_XX scale with n, and C depends on the weights. The bound is not shown to reduce to the n-independent O(m exp(-alpha m^{1/d})) form that is advertised as carrying over 'automatically'. No eigenvalue-decay argument for the normal-cycle point sets is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the guarantee in the form actually proved, with the explicit n/S factor and C, and the stretched-exponential eigenvalue decay for Gaussian kernels in dimension d, or add a short argument for the n-independent form.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised rate form and the 'exponential in m' statement are not what the stated bound supports. The dependence of the guarantee on n and on the weight magnitude is hidden.
issues.title: Compression rate claimed as exponential in m and carried over without the prefactors in the stated bound
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the rate with its true dependence on n and C preserves the method and the theorem. Only the advertised summary changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims the compressed and uncompressed Queen matchings have almost identical quality, evidenced by a near-identical Hausdorff score. The reported values are 0.0442 (full) and 0.0298 (compressed), a difference of about 33-48% of either value. This is not 'near identical', and the single Hausdorff number does not support the claim that the matchings are almost identical, since the matching quality is measured only by this metric. The conclusion's 'negligible difference in registration quality' relies on this.

failure_location.quote: This is numerically evidenced by the near identical Hausdorff metric score.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the Queen result accurately (compressed matching has a lower Hausdorff distance) and restrict the 'near identical' wording to the Pumpkin case or support it with additional metrics.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical evidence for 'negligible difference' in matching quality is misstated for the Queen case. Only the Pumpkin case (0.1621 vs 0.1662) supports it.
issues.title: Queen experiment described as near-identical Hausdorff score although the reported values differ substantially
issues.why_classification: The fix is a rewording of the claim against the reported numbers. It does not alter any theorem, algorithm or the qualitative conclusion that compression does not hurt.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is a consistent approximation \cite{NCpaper}, as the edge-lengths tend to zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The cylindrical Dirac weights come from replacing the integral over an edge by |e| times the integrand at the edge midpoint. This is explicitly only an approximation that becomes consistent as edge length goes to 0. NC_delta nevertheless writes it as an equality with N(T). Theorem 3 bounds only the distance between the discrete functional mu (the delta form) and its Nystrom compression. No bound is given for the distance between mu and N(T), or between N(T) and the normal cycle of the smooth underlying shape. The conclusion's guarantee 'to the true underlying shape' therefore does not follow from what is proved.

failure_location.quote: guarantees of small RKHS distance to the normal cycle of the true underlying shape

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the discrete delta functional and state that the delta form is an approximation of N(T). Optionally add a discretisation-error bound or cite one precisely.
issues.overall_effect: The end-to-end guarantee of the abstract and conclusion is stronger than the paper establishes. It covers only the compression error relative to the discretised (midpoint) delta form.
issues.title: Guarantee claimed relative to the true underlying shape, but the delta form is only a midpoint approximation of N(T) and the discretisation error is never controlled
issues.why_classification: The result survives only as a weaker, clearly scoped statement that withdraws the claimed guarantee to the true shape. Recovering the stronger claim would need an additional error analysis.
